x: Next on the track with Bels now in a one point lead were the 10,000m boys. A comfortable win by Amos Seddon over Bill Sutherland left Ray Middleton to come in fourth and Len Duquemin 5th.
Winner on this warm afternoon was Amos Seddon with Ray Middleton strolling in behind. Lou Mockett grabbed 3rd place from John Moullin on the last lap round the Common.

Shaun Lightman took the lead after 3 miles and was never headed whilst Carl retook Amos Seddon for 3rd. Leicester packed their first three in nine but we powered in by one point with our usual scoring four despite the return of Allan Callow, and Ray Middleton leaving the road at one time to water the flowers.

The next race, the 10,000 metres saw John Bromley complete his preparation for the World Veteran's Championships in Canada by finishing 3rd to British Internationals Amos Seddon (Enfield) and Stuart Maidment (Yeovil Olympiads).

Graham had just over half a minute on Carl at the finish of the 10Km. 44:43 to 45:15, with Amos Seddon (BoE) a further five seconds down. Other Belgrave placings were: 10.J.Hall 48:06; 15.R.Middleton 48:59; 26.J.Dunsford 53:08; 34.R.Day 54:36; 37.D.Fotheringham 55:31; 42.S.

These were the team scores in this year's G.L.C. 10 miles Walking Championship of Ilford AC (without Roger Mills), Belgrave and Enfield (without Amos Seddon), with Surrey WC not far behind with 42 points.
The result was a great win for Graham Seatter who finished nearly three minutes ahead of his old rivals Roger Mills (Ilford) and Amos Seddon (Boro' of Enfield).
To the race itself, the early leaders were Olly Flynn, Mike Parker, Brian Adams and Amos Seddon with Carl not too far back. The team race looked good for Ilford A.C. who had many well up.

Two individual victories were recorded by Richard Dorman and Carl Lawton both of whom had been up the previous Friday night on the Ewhurst 100. Senior Mens 15kms: 1.C.Lawton 69.13; 2.A.Seddon (Enfield) 69.46; 10.J.Newnham 76.02; 14.M.Nicholls 76.45; 19.J.Bromley 82.06;
